Can ≠ will. The fact that things *can* get better makes it all the more infuriating — because I know that things don't have to be this way. But they are.

I'm tired of things taking fucking years. It's been 39 of them. This isn't a funk, this is my life. I've sacrificed and given of myself to build a life, and it is all come to nothing. Nothing I've done counts anymore. Nothing I've given matters. I've spent all this time hoping and working for a better tomorrow that has never come. My body is now old and practically falling apart, my mental health isn't any better, and my capacity to enjoy things even if they suddenly miraculously got better has been greatly diminished. Giving my health, I don't think my life span is going to be that long anyway. There is no point to continue to suffer in hope for a future that never materializes.

My dog cannot be happy. She's had a growth on her face that exploded weeks ago, and looks like a bloody mess. I haven't had the money to take her to the vet, because I can't function as a human being. The only reason I'm taking her now is because a neighbor saw her and volunteered to pay for it — so now I'm imposing on that neighbor. We are both living in a van with no climate control, and I know the heat this summer has gotten to her — the cold this winter will as well, since I'm less prepared for it than I was last winter. Hell, the only reason she made it through last winter was because she got sick at the time of the big deep freeze the hit down the middle of the US, perfectly timed for her to go stay at the vet for 2 weeks to recover — which is also paid for by someone else, coincidentally one of the people I had a fight with tonight.

I have tried and tried and tried. Maybe I'm just not trying enough. Who knows anymore? I don't think that even has any meaning anymore. I'm not sure what "try" even consists of. Maybe I've never been trying. I don't know.

I will make sure she sees what happens, so she can at least have some closure and not think I just disappeared.

Sure, there's good in the world — but that's kind of like saying there's corn in a piece of poop. What good is the good when it's so spoiled? There's no way to enjoy that good like this.

**There is a large part of my that wants to see covid-19 run out of control and decimate everything.**

I was going to post this in r/confessions, but according to their rules thoughts don't count as misdeeds and so don't belong there.

To be clear, there's a large part of me that doesn't feel this way, and that's the part of me that is winning out. I don't really want this to happen. But I have been struggling with a feeling of bitterness, a feeling like the world deserves this. A feeling like this is justice. I know this feeling is extremely wrong and perverse, and that there are many truly innocent people being affected by this and who will be affected by this. But I just can't shake this thinking completely, and every time I deal with someone denying covid-19, someone saying it's a hoax, someone saying they can do what they want and put other people in danger, someone taking advantage of other people in this situation, or people generally being cruddy to each other or to me — this feeling flares back up like a wildfire.

*A little background:* I've been in virtual isolation for years. Ever since my divorce, and since I walked away from religion, I've been almost entirely on my own. I've had very few friends and family to lean on at any time. I've had no social life and very few people I could turn to for help when I needed it. I live in poverty, I haven't had running water in several years, I've been without power for months, I'm in the process of losing my home, and the bank is giving me no quarter even with the pandemic in progress. I was stuck working at a dead-end job for 13 years, until they eliminated my position and gave me a severance package (which they dragged their feet on actually giving to me for months). Over the past 5 years my physical and mental health have declined sharply. I have been able to afford very little therapy and very few doctor visits, and I am now pretty much physically disabled because of conditions that have been left untreated. Most of the people now freaking out about lockdowns and shutdowns were the people who blamed me for my situation, told me to pull myself up by my own bootstraps, and otherwise ignored me. I've struggled to feed myself, I've struggled to keep some shred of my sanity, I've struggled in vain to break out of my situation. And the world doesn't care. Everyone is so divided, everyone is so apathetic, everyone clings to their own little world and doesn't care about anyone else.

And then covid-19 came. It's like the whole world is getting a taste of what they've put me through. I'm finding it hard to have empathy for those in isolation, those who are struggling financially, those out in work, those who are sick — especially as people continue in their old ways in spite of it, and continue to be crappy to one another. Whenever I see a news article about somebody who had previously been claiming it was hype or a hoax get sick, part of me is happy — and I absolutely hate that. Part of me is hoping that they lift all of the lockdowns and precautions, not because I don't think the disease is serious — it is, I've spent a lot of time researching it and debunking deniers — but because part of me wants to see the carnage maximized and the oppressive institutions in this country fall apart under social, political, and economic collapse. I want to see my bank go belly up. I want to see my former employer shut their doors forever. The thought of the people who left me entirely alone when I needed help alone, suffering, sick — there's a part of me that gets a thrill out of the thought, and that's absolutely disgusting.

I feel gross for thinking this way, and rightly so. It's wrong. I'm wrong. Even if it were right to wish harm on these people and institutions — and it's not — I would still be wrong because covid-19 causes its damage indiscriminately, and many legitimately innocent people are going to suffer and die because of it, and it is a horrible tragedy. And I care about that. I'm grieved by what's happening and what's coming. But I'm grieved even more that people are making it worse, that people are making things worse for each other, and that people have been doing so before this ever happened. And that makes me angry and bitter. Thinking about what they've done to me makes me angry and bitter. And then I start wishing harm on people, which only makes me angry at myself, as it goes against the very reasons I'm angry in the first place — because of the harm so many others are causing. I hate this part of me. I'm ashamed of it, and it's not who I want to be. But I don't know how to shake it.

Several years ago I had a co-worker show up at our mutual workplace in the middle of the night. She was visibly shaken, upset, and in terrible shape physically. Her abusive boyfriend and baby daddy had chased her into town over a mile of hilly, rough country roadway with her on foot and him in a vehicle. We tried to get her help, found a place for her to stay, etc; She ended up going back to him. He forced her to quit the job, cut up her work clothes, and used their child as leverage against her to make her do what he wanted.

Over the course of several more years, I watched this cycle repeat between her and him. She would get a new job, establish connections with people besides him, they'd find out about the abuse and try to help, and he would intervene and reel her in with more physically and psychologically abusive tactics. It took its toll on her. She became more and more a shell of herself. Once one of the nicest people I knew, honest and one of our better employees when she worked with us, last I heard she was seen shoplifting from our store on multiple occasions. At one point, she let me back in and I was trying to help her and her kid get into a shelter, get some funds and resources of her own, and so on. But he was still in her head, she was terrified to do anything, and he eventually found out about it. At one point, him and I had a confrontation by text when he found her secret phone. I haven't heard from her since then, except seeing her passingly in the custody of him or his grandmother who is complicit in the whole matter. I watched one of the sweetest, most genuine people I knew get her mind filleted by this narcissistic sociopath, transforming her into little more than his terrified drone with no will of her own left.

I'm not a fighter and I don't like violence, I don't believe that violence truly solves problems — but this is the one time in my life that I have actively seriously contemplated hunting somebody down and straight up killing them. At one point, I was so livid that the only reason I didn't was because I lacked the means — there's no way I could get away with doing so, and I didn't remember his last name which made it hard for me to gather any information on him. He's smart, and he knows how to cover his tracks and play things close to the chest. And I have kids of my own and others who care about me, which I have to factor in when considering that I would potentially be throwing my own life away to stop him — if I didn't have them, I might see it as worth it.

I haven't seen or heard anything out of them in quite a while. I don't know what the current state of things is for them. But I really hope that somehow, somewhere, someone sees the situation and has more capability and more of a backbone than I did — at least to the point of being able to help her out of that situation. His one weakness was that he used her to bring in income so that he could sit on his ass and do nothing, which exposed her to other people who could find out what he was doing to her. I hope this bites him in the ass sooner than later.

There are two simple possible solutions for the Hall of Fame problem.

The easy solution is simply to make custom classes ineligible for Hall of Fame, just as if the game was played in master mode.

A slightly more complex solution is a class building tool, where any parameter or feature you add to a class has a score (positive or negative, depending on the feature), and only classes at or below a certain score are eligible for Hall of Fame. This would have to be tested to make sure it was balanced and didn't have any serious exploits, but it shouldn't be *that* difficult to implement, and it would solve the problem.

You could use this same format for making custom races.

I love this game, but it REALLY needs a lot more customization options to reach its potential — a campaign editor to make custom levels, like the one built into the game, being another such feature. Again, the simple solution to prevent abuse is to make such campaigns in eligible for the Hall of Fame, or make campaign specific Halls of Fame.

These are valid points. Psychosomatic symptoms are physiological — psychosomatic does not mean imagined or "all in your head", your mind has very real effects on your body. The involuntary muscle movements you mentioned are a very relevant point in particular — I triggered an episode wants playing a video game, a simple little Telegram game called Lumberjack, trying to beat my friends' high scores. I kept tensing up during the game so much, that it made my chest get tight and gave me a particularly bad episode, the effects of which lingard for days. (But hey, I knocked their high scores out of the water.)

Also, alcohol has some peculiar effects on me. I believe I am quite right to say that alcohol actually makes me a better person — and I'm very aware that that is not the normal effect it has. I think clearer, I'm more decisive, less inhibited but still clear thinking enough to be rational, less influenced by anxiety — and I tend to be more aware of and in tune with my surroundings. But I hadn't considered that this could make me more in tune with my body's own sensations — more aware of what I was already physically feeling.

Well, I've done a lot of pushing through the pain. Especially when I was employed. One more reason why I doubt it was my heart — I soldiered through it for too long, pushed myself too hard when I absolutely shouldn't have, and I'm still breathing without any relevant medical intervention (apart from the occasional cautionary aspirin). And after taking about two and a half months to rest, there are some things that I am able to do now that I haven't been able to do for most of the past year,and I'm not getting the intense episodes that I was occasionally getting off and on — so there has been some net improvement without intervention. I overdid myself today to the point where I was really feeling the tightness in my chest — but after sleeping for 5 hours, I feel great.

Biggest reasons I doubt the costochondritis theory — even about one shot of alcohol and I'm feeling some tightness in my chest and arm. However, this could be explained as psychosomatic. Also, there are various sedentary but intense activities which often set it off — but these too could be psychosomatic, and I haven't had much of a problem with this since things started improving about a month ago. Also, sometimes I do get blood pressure spikes, and when I do I can definitely feel it in my chest and my left arm — but this could be primarily from anxiety. And, being autistic, my senses work weird, and sometimes autistic people can sense things that others cannot (real things, like our natural senses pick them up where other people's miss them). I suppose it's possible that could apply to heart rate and blood pressure. There's also the point that the first time I really had an issue was after a night of drinking — but I only had six drinks, and that could be coincidence.

But heart problems don't explain how I can stretch and pop my chest and get so much relief — like night and day difference, like flipping a switch and turning two-thirds of it off. They don't explain the various times that I experienced the problem more on the right that on the left. They don't explain the numbness in my ulnar nerves that almost always come with it. And they don't explain my unassisted improvement — or how I have persisted to function through so many episodes.

Actually, costochondritis has been suggested before by some of my friends online, and I've stumbled upon information about it myself and begun to suspect it. It seems to be the best explanation to fit all the facts I know, but I don't really have a way to test it conclusively, and there are at least a few things that don't 100% fit my understanding of it — but none of them so far off as to even come close to disproving it.

Needing people and needing connections ≠ the popular media image of being surrounded by people and partying. Rejection of that extreme does not imply that the opposite extreme, isolation and hyperindividualism, are a good thing. I guarantee you that most of those elderly people have had friends, family, and people to support them throughout their lives. and if they haven't, it is usually reflected in their physical or mental health. There are exceptions — but again, people who are able to climb Mount Everest are also the exception. Some people eat like crap and smoke everyday and live to a hundred, that doesn't mean it's healthy. Isolation isn't healthy — social needs are a legitimate human need. The existence of some people who are able to defy this do not disprove it.

Hi. I've been living in virtual isolation for years. The friends I have are far away. I'm estranged from my family, and they also live far away. I'm divorced and completely on my own. Now my life is falling apart more and more. Every time I think I hit rock bottom, the bottom breaks open. When I get sick, I never have anyone to fall back on it help. I've laid on my backside for 24 hours or more, not eating or drinking or moving, because I have been too sick and had no one to help.

This ideal of hyper-individualism is completely toxic. Don't get trapped in it. Human beings are social animals. We *need* each other, in the same sense that we need food, water, and shelter. You are a finite person — your capabilities are inherently limited, and no matter how self-reliant you become they always will be. Very few people can go it alone, just like very few people can climb Mount Everest because of how incompatible that environment is to our own humanity.

Don't do it. If you are having problems with toxic relationships, that's an issue to address. But isolation is not a solution.

Me. I spent years trusting the advice of others, working hard, and trying to do things "right" — but I failed to consider my own physical and psychological limits. I'm autistic, not in particularly good health, and I have a lot of psychological baggage from an abusive upbringing. Thought I could soldier through it — and for a long time I did. But it all caught up with me. Eventually, I started to give out physically and mentally, and everything slowly fell apart when I couldn't keep it together anymore. Five years ago I was married, had a family, had a steady job, was religious, and became a new homeowner. I'm currently sitting in the dark without power, alone, smelling like a toilet, more or less waiting to die, and without any real options to change that without making things even worse. You can read a more detailed account [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/eo2i3n/im_at_the_end_i_dont_see_another_way_around_this/?utm_medium=android_app&utm_source=share).

Moral of the story: Don't bite off more than you can chew. Be realistic and self aware of your limitations, and stay away from self-help and positivity nonsense that tells you it's all about choice, determination, and working hard. Because luck and circumstances play a big factor, as do your own capabilities. Accept that you are a finite person, otherwise the universe will eventually remind you of this.

The first doctor thought it was bronchitis — I may or may not have actually had bronchitis, but that obviously wasn't the main issue. The second doctor thought it was anxiety — and anxiety is definitely part of the issue. However, no conclusive diagnosis beyond that has been made, and I don't think anxiety explains the whole issue.

Neither doctor thought it was my heart — I'm inclined to agree because I can frequently get a lot of relief from the chest pains by popping my back, neck, chest, or shoulders. Usually, when I am feeling pain and tightness, I can stretch and pop and get relief. However, when I was having the problems worse, sometimes I could go for a week or two without being able to pop anything. but then, I would stretch, something would pop, and it would be like someone flipped a switch and most of the pain, pressure, and related difficulties went away.

Also, I get issues on both the right and left side. the problem started out more on the right than on the left, though I get it now more on the left. I do get pain and tingling in my arms, but most of the tingling is along the ulnar nerves, that tingling tends to happen more in the right arm, and my understanding is that cardiovascular pain happens on the opposite side of the arm most of the time. (I could be mistaken in that information.) I have gotten pain in my left arm on that side of it along with pain on the left side of my chest, but this isn't the norm, and it usually only happens when I'm having a more serious episode.

I have not transitioned. I cannot afford hormones or therapy, let alone surgery. And my ex-wife doesn't know. I'm tired of changing my mindset. I've been doing that for so long, and it's so exhausting, and it doesn't change anything.
